entries.name: OPEN CONTAINER INITIATIVE
entries.description: The Open Container Initiative is a lightweight, open governance structure, to be formed under the auspices of the Linux Foundation, for the express purpose of creating open industry standards around container formats and runtime.

entries.name: Cloud Native Computing Foundation
entries.description: The Cloud Native Computing Foundation will create and drive the adoption of a new set of common container technologies informed by technical merit and end user value, and inspired by Internet-scale computing.

entries.name: Cloud Foundry Foundation
entries.description: The Cloud is our foundry.

entries.name: Open Container Specifications
entries.description: This project is where the Open Container Initiative Specifications are written. This is a work in progress.

entries.name: App Container basics
entries.description: App Container (appc) is an open specification that defines several aspects of how to run applications in containers: an image format, runtime environment, and discovery protocol.

entries.name: Systemd Container Interface
entries.description: Systemd is a suite of basic building blocks for a Linux system. It provides a system and service manager that runs as PID 1 and starts the rest of the system. If you write a container solution, please consider supporting the following interfaces.

entries.name: Nulecule Specification
entries.description: Nulecule defines a pattern and model for packaging complex multi-container applications and services, referencing all their dependencies, including orchestration metadata in a container image for building, deploying, monitoring, and active management.

entries.name: Oracle microcontainer manifesto
entries.description: This is not a new container format, but simply a specific method for constructing a container that allows for better security and stability.

entries.name: Cloud Native Application Bundle Specification
entries.description: A package format specification that describes a technology for bundling, installing, and managing distributed applications, that are by design, cloud agnostic.

entries.name: Amazon EC2 Container Service
entries.description: Container management service that supports Docker containers and allows you to easily run applications on a managed cluster of Amazon EC2 instances.

entries.name: Google Cloud Platform
entries.description: Run Docker containers on Google Cloud Platform, powered by Kubernetes. Google Container Engine actively schedules your containers, based on declared needs, on a managed cluster of virtual machines.

entries.name: Jelastic
entries.description: Unlimited PaaS and Container-Based IaaS in a Joint Cloud Solution for DevOps.

entries.name: Joyent
entries.description: High-Performance Container-Native Infrastructure for Today's Demanding Real-Time Web and Mobile Applications.

entries.name: Kubernetes
entries.description: Manage a cluster of Linux containers as a single system to accelerate Dev and simplify Ops.

entries.name: Mesosphere
entries.description: The Mesosphere Datacenter Operating System (DCOS) is a new kind of operating system that spans all of the machines in your datacenter or cloud. It provides a highly elastic, and highly scalable way of deploying applications, services and big data infrastructure on shared resources.

entries.name: OpenShift Origin
entries.description: OpenShift Origin is a distribution of Kubernetes optimized for continuous application development and multi-tenant deployment. Origin adds developer and operations-centric tools on top of Kubernetes to enable rapid application development, easy deployment and scaling, and long-term lifecycle maintenance for small and large teams.

entries.name: Warden
entries.description: Manages isolated, ephemeral, and resource controlled environments. Part of Cloud Foundry - the open platform as a service project.

entries.name: Virtuozzo
entries.description: A platform, built on Virtuozzo containers, that can be easily run on top of any bare-metal or virtual servers in any public or private cloud, to automate, optimize, and accelerate internal IT and development processes.

entries.name: Rancher
entries.description: Rancher is a complete, open source platform for deploying and managing containers in production. It includes commercially-supported distributions of Kubernetes, Mesos, and Docker Swarm, making it easy to run containerized applications on any infrastructure.

entries.name: Docker Swarm
entries.description: Docker Swarm is native clustering for Docker.

entries.name: Azure Container Service
entries.description: Azure Container Service optimizes the configuration of popular open source tools and technologies specifically for Azure.

entries.name: CIAO
entries.description: Cloud Integrated Advanced Orchestrator for Intel Clear Linux OS.

entries.name: Alibaba Cloud Container Service
entries.description: Container Service is a high-performance and scalable container application management service that enables you to use Docker and Kubernetes to manage the lifecycle of containerized applications.

entries.name: Nomad
entries.description: HashiCorp Nomad is a single binary that schedules applications and services on Linux, Windows, and Mac. It is an open source scheduler that uses a declarative job file for scheduling virtualized, containerized, and standalone applications.

entries.name: CoreOs
entries.description: A lightweight Linux operating system designed for clustered deployments providing automation, security, and scalability for your most critical applications.

entries.name: RancherOS
entries.description: RancherOS is a tiny Linux distro that runs the entire OS as Docker containers.

entries.name: Project Atomic
entries.description: Project Atomic provides the best platform for your Linux Docker Kubernetes (LDK) application stack. Use immutable infrastructure to deploy and scale your containerized applications.

entries.name: Snappy Ubuntu Core
entries.description: Ubuntu Core is the perfect system for large-scale cloud container deployments, bringing transactional updates to the world’s favourite container platform.

entries.name: ResinOS
entries.description: A host OS tailored for containers, designed for reliability, proven in production.

entries.name: Photon
entries.description: Photon OS is a minimal Linux container host designed to have a small footprint and tuned for VMware platforms. Photon is intended to invite collaboration around running containerized and Linux applications in a virtualized environment.

entries.name: Clear Linux Project
entries.description: The Clear Linux Project for Intel Architecture is a distribution built for various Cloud use cases.

entries.name: CargOS
entries.description: CargOS is a new lightweight, open source, platform for Docker hosts that aims for speed, manageability and security. Releases are built for 64-bit Intel/AMD CPUs.

entries.name: OSv
entries.description: OSv is the open source operating system designed for the cloud. Built from the ground up for effortless deployment and management, with superior performance.

entries.name: HypriotOS
entries.description: Minimal Debian-based operating systems that is optimized to run Docker. It made it dead easy use Docker on any Raspberry Pi.

entries.name: MCL
entries.description: MCL (Minimal Container Linux) is a from scratch minimal Linux OS designed specifically to run containers. It has a small footprint of ~50MB and boots within seconds. It is currently optimized to run Docker.

entries.name: Docker
entries.description: An open platform for distributed applications for developers and sysadmins. Standard de facto.

entries.name: LXD
entries.description: Daemon based on liblxc offering a REST API to manage LXC containers.

entries.name: OpenVZ
entries.description: OpenVZ is container-based virtualization for Linux. OpenVZ creates multiple secure, isolated Linux containers (otherwise known as VEs or VPSs) on a single physical server enabling better server utilization and ensuring that applications do not conflict.

entries.name: MultiDocker
entries.description: Create a secure multi-user Docker machine, where each user is segregated into an indepentent container.

entries.name: Lithos
entries.description: Lithos is a process supervisor and containerizer for running services. It is not intended to be system init, but rather tries to be a base tool to build container orchestration.

entries.name: containerd
entries.description: A container runtime which can manage a complete container lifecycle - from image transfer/storage to container execution, supervision and networking.

entries.name: runc
entries.description: runc is a CLI tool for spawning and running containers according to the OCS specification.

entries.name: Bocker
entries.description: Docker implemented in around 100 lines of bash.

entries.name: Rocket
entries.description: rkt (pronounced "rock-it") is a CLI for running app containers on Linux. rkt is designed to be composable, secure, and fast. Based on AppC specification.

entries.name: LXC
entries.description: LXC is the well known set of tools, templates, library and language bindings. It's pretty low level, very flexible and covers just about every containment feature supported by the upstream kernel.

entries.name: Vagga
entries.description: Vagga is a fully-userspace container engine inspired by Vagrant and Docker, specialized for development environments.

entries.name: libct
entries.description: Libct is a containers management library which provides convenient API for frontend programs to rule a container during its whole lifetime.

entries.name: libvirt
entries.description: A big toolkit to interact with the virtualization capabilities of recent versions of Linux (and other OSes).

entries.name: systemd-nspawn
entries.description: Spawn a namespace container for debugging, testing and building. Part of systemd.

entries.name: porto
entries.description: The main goal of Porto is to create a convenient, reliable interface over several Linux kernel mechanism such as cgroups, namespaces, mounts, networking etc.

entries.name: udocker
entries.description: A basic user tool to execute simple containers in batch or interactive systems without root privileges.

entries.name: Let Me Contain That For You
entries.description: LMCTFY is the open source version of Google’s container stack, which provides Linux application containers.

entries.name: cc-oci-runtime
entries.description: Intel Clear Linux OCI (Open Containers Initiative) compatible runtime.

entries.name: railcar
entries.description: Railcar is a rust implementation of the opencontainers initiative's runtime spec. It is similar to the reference implementation runc, but it is implemented completely in rust for memory safety without needing the overhead of a garbage collector or multiple threads.

entries.name: Kata Containers
entries.description: Kata Containers is a new open source project building extremely lightweight virtual machines that seamlessly plug into the containers ecosystem.

entries.name: plash
entries.description: Lightweight, rootless containers.

entries.name: runv
entries.description: Hypervisor-based (KVM, Xen, QEMU) Runtime for OCI. Security by isolation.

entries.name: podman
entries.description: Full management of container lifecycle.

entries.name: firecracker
entries.description: Firecracker runs workloads in lightweight virtual machines, called microVMs, which combine the security and isolation properties provided by hardware virtualization technology with the speed and flexibility of containers.

entries.name: sysbox
entries.description: Sysbox is a "runc" that creates secure (rootless) containers / pods that run not just microservices, but most workloads that run in VMs (e.g., systemd, Docker, and Kubernetes), seamlessly.

entries.name: youki
entries.description: A container runtime written in Rust.

entries.name: footloose
entries.description: Containers that look like Virtual Machines.

entries.name: Firejail
entries.description: Firejail is a SUID sandbox program that reduces the risk of security breaches by restricting the running environment of untrusted applications using Linux namespaces, seccomp-bpf and Linux capabilities.

entries.name: NsJail
entries.description: NsJail is a process isolation tool for Linux. It makes use of the namespacing, resource control, and seccomp-bpf syscall filter subsystems of the Linux kernel.

entries.name: Subuser
entries.description: Securing the Linux desktop with Docker.

entries.name: Snappy
entries.description: Snappy Ubuntu Core is a new rendition of Ubuntu with transactional updates - a minimal server image with the same libraries as today’s Ubuntu, but applications are provided through a simpler mechanism.

entries.name: xdg-app
entries.description: xdg-app is a system for building, distributing and running sandboxed desktop applications on Linux.

entries.name: Bubblewrap
entries.description: Run applications in a sandbox using Linux namespaces without root privileges, with user namespacing provided via setuid binary.

entries.name: singularity
entries.description: Universal application containers for Linux.

entries.name: Lxroot
entries.description: Lxroot is a flexible, lightweight, and safer alternative to chroot and/or Docker for non-root users on Linux.

entries.name: nsenter
entries.description: Run program with namespaces of other processes. Part of the util-linux.

entries.name: ip-netns
entries.description: Process network namespace management. Part of the iproute2.

entries.name: unshare
entries.description: Run program with some namespaces unshared from parent. Part of the util-linux.

entries.name: python-nsenter
entries.description: This Python package allows entering Linux kernel namespaces (mount, IPC, net, PID, user and UTS) by doing the "setns" syscall.

entries.name: butter
entries.description: Python library to interface to low level linux features (inotify, fanotify, timerfd, signalfd, eventfd, containers) with asyncio support.

entries.name: pyspaces
entries.description: Works with Linux namespaces through glibc with pure python.

entries.name: CRIU
entries.description: Checkpoint/Restore In Userspace is a software tool for Linux operating system. Using this tool, you can freeze a running application (or part of it) and checkpoint it to a hard drive as a collection of files. CRIU integrated with Docker and LXC to implement Live migration of containers.

entries.name: Moby
entries.description: A "Lego set" of toolkit components for containers software created by Docker.

entries.name: container-diff
entries.description: A tool for analyzing and comparing container images.

entries.name: buildah
entries.description: A tool which facilitates building OCI container images.

entries.name: skopeo
entries.description: Work with remote images registries - retrieving information, images, signing content.

entries.name: img
entries.description: Standalone, daemon-less, unprivileged Dockerfile and OCI compatible container image builder.

entries.name: dgr
entries.description: Command line utility designed to build and to configure at runtime App Containers Images (ACI) and App Container Pods (POD) based on convention over configuration.

entries.name: Whaler
entries.description: Whaler is designed to reverse engineer a Docker Image into the Dockerfile that created it.

entries.name: dive
entries.description: A tool for exploring each layer in a docker image.

entries.name: go-containerregistry
entries.description: Go library and CLIs for working with container registries.

entries.name: kaniko
entries.description: Kaniko is a tool to build container images from a Dockerfile, inside a container or Kubernetes cluster.

entries.name: umoci
entries.description: Umoci is a tool to manipulate OCI container images, and can be used as a rudimentary build tool.

entries.name: docker pushrm
entries.description: A Docker CLI plugin that that lets you push the README.md file from the current directory to a container registry. Supports Docker Hub, Quay and Harbor.

entries.name: LXC-Web-Panel
entries.description: Web panel for LXC on Ubuntu.

entries.name: Liman
entries.description: Basic docker monitoring web application.

entries.name: portainer
entries.description: Lightweight Docker management UI.

entries.name: swarmpit
entries.description: Lightweight mobile-friendly Docker Swarm management UI.

entries.name: The Twelve-Factor App
entries.description: The twelve-factor app is a methodology for building software-as-a-service apps.

entries.name: Container Best Practices
entries.description: A collaborative project to document container-based application architecture, creation and management from Project Atomic.

entries.name: Docker bench security
entries.description: The Docker Bench for Security is a script that checks for dozens of common best-practices around deploying Docker containers in production.

entries.name: CoreOS Clair
entries.description: Open Source Vulnerability Analysis for your Containers.

entries.name: bane
entries.description: Custom AppArmor profile generator for docker containers.

entries.name: OpenSCAP
entries.description: The OpenSCAP ecosystem provides multiple tools to assist administrators and auditors with assessment, measurement and enforcement of security baselines.

entries.name: drydock
entries.description: Drydock provides a flexible way of assessing the security of your Docker daemon configuration and containers using editable audit templates.

entries.name: trireme
entries.description: Security by segmentation for Docker and Kubernetes.

entries.name: goss
entries.description: Quick and Easy server testing/validation.

entries.name: sockguard
entries.description: A proxy for docker.sock that enforces access control and isolated privileges.

entries.name: gvisor
entries.description: gVisor is a user-space kernel, written in Go, that implements a substantial portion of the Linux system surface. It includes an Open Container Initiative (OCI) runtime called runsc that provides an isolation boundary between the application and the host kernel. The runsc runtime integrates with Docker and Kubernetes, making it simple to run sandboxed containers.

entries.name: docker-explorer
entries.description: A tool to help forensicate offline docker acquisitions.

entries.name: oci-seccomp-bpf-hook
entries.description: OCI hook to trace syscalls and generate a seccomp profile.

sysdig-container-ecosystem
entries.description: The ecosystem of awesome new technologies emerging around containers and microservices can be a little overwhelming, to say the least. We thought we might be able to help: welcome to the Container Ecosystem Project.

entries.name: doger.io
entries.description: This page is an attempt to document the ins and outs of containers on Linux. This is not just restricted to programmers looking to implement containers or use container like features in their own code but also Sysadmins and Users who want to get more of a handle on how containers work 'under the hood'.
